text:
zara: Heads up  merged cust/pagoda/lora-v1 and pushed an int4 q4f build to canary. Quick retrieval eval (billing-lookup quickpack) shows sharp ranking drift. Starting triage.

pete: Drop the tag + quick numbers?

zara: Tag: pagoda-lora-v1-q4f (LoRA merge -> bnb q4f quant). Eval cmd: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite billing-lookup --model pagoda-lora-v1-q4f --batch 160 --cache on
```
Metrics: recall@10 0.53 (int8 baseline 0.80), mrr 0.09 (baseline 0.20), p@1 0.60 (baseline 0.84), median_latency 35ms (baseline 50ms). Lots of top-3 swaps.

anil: Any tokenizer/preproc diffs in the PR?

zara: Nope  adapter-only merge. Quant config used: 
```
quant_backend: bnb
quant_mode: q4f
adapter_only: true
per_layer_scaling: true
```
Tried cache toggles and warm-prefix; regression persists.

ci-bot: Regression ticket RG-2028-0610-09 opened: https://issues.redwood.ai/RG-2028-0610-09

pete: My hunch  bnb-q4f per-layer scaling moves adapter projection outputs. Quick experiments: 1) rerun with `--quant-backend nf4` 2) q4f with `per_layer_scaling=false` 3) try `--adapter-aware-quantizer`. I'll run a small grid.

ops-bot: Canary deployed: canary/pagoda -> pagoda-lora-v1-q4f (pool: canary-us-3)

pete: NF4 quick run done: recall@10 0.75, mrr 0.18, p@1 0.80, latency ~37ms. Much better but slight gap to int8.

anil: Good. Which adapter layers look sensitive? Can we do a layerwise scan?

zara: Running layer-scan: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite billing-lookup --model pagoda-lora-v1-q4f --layer-scan true --quant-backend bnb --output /tmp/pagoda-layer-scan.json
```

zara: Layer-scan summary: adapter projection layers 2 and 5 show the biggest displacement with bnb-q4f+per-layer-scaling. Low-rank adapter outputs are getting overscaled.

pete: If nf4 recovers most quality, propose immediate rollback of canary traffic to int8, and change the CUST quant pipeline to prefer `nf4` for adapter-only quant or enable adapter-aware quantizer by default. Also add a quickpack embedding-drift gate in LoRA CI.

anil: Agreed. I'll draft the pipeline patch and a unit test asserting recall@10 drop < 0.03 vs int8 on billing-lookup.

zara: Rollback command: `rwi-deploy promote --model pagoda-lora-v1-int8 --route canary/pagoda --reason "restore retrieval quality"`

ops-bot: Deployment event: promoted pagoda-lora-v1-int8 -> canary/pagoda (change id: DPL-15101)

ci-bot: RG-2028-0610-09 status -> triaged (severity: high). Artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/evals/pagoda/1887654321-grid.json

pete: I'll attach the grid artifacts (q4f vs nf4 x per_layer_scaling true/false x adapter-aware) to the PR. Also will run a couple of random-seed reruns to ensure nf4 stability.

anil: I'll take the bnb scale math follow-up (check calibration step & per-layer scale heuristics).

zara: CS notified, draft message prepared (brief explanation + mitigation + ETA 24-48h). We'll smoke billing-lookup after PR merges.

pete: Quick follow-up note: nf4 latency is ~2-3ms higher in our canary env but quality tradeoff is worth it for customers. Include that in PR.

zara: Thanks all. End thread for now.
